solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Filthy hole turned dry, swallowing water? (7)

indicatorNotes.turned: something turned round faces the other way, so SEC is read backwards

blocks.note: sec = dry, of wine; turned, it reads CES
spit is the water in your mouth, the kind you swallow

annotation.surface: Someone describes a dried-up, dirty hole that has taken in water.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the loose definition of SPIT: it is mouth-water, the stuff one swallows.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: a cesspit is a pit for sewage, about as filthy as holes get.

entries.clue: Policeman delayed collecting guilty American’s print (11)

indicatorNotes.collecting: to collect something is to gather it in, so COP and LATE take PERP between them

blocks.note: perp = perpetrator, US police slang for the guilty party

annotation.surface: A late-running policeman picks up an American suspect's fingerprints.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Print' in the surface is a fingerprint; the answer is a style of engraving and the neat handwriting copied from it.
annotation.definitionFit: A kind of print: copperplate is printing from engraved copper plates, and the formal script modelled on it.

entries.clue: Dram of type drunkard says? (5)

indicatorNotes.drunkard says: a drunk slurs his words, thickening an S into SH

blocks.note: sort = type, spoken with a drunken slur

annotation.surface: A drunk asks for his usual kind of dram.
annotation.walkthrough: The sound change is a drunk's slur rather than a true homophone: SORT with the S thickened to SH.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a short is a small measure of spirits, like a dram of whisky.

entries.clue: Hold good bucket that vicar fills (7)

indicatorNotes.fills: whatever fills a bucket goes inside it, so REV goes into PAIL

blocks.note: Rev, short for Reverend, a vicar's title

annotation.surface: A parishioner is told to keep a good bucket that the vicar has filled.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hold good' reads as an instruction to keep the bucket, but it is one phrase meaning 'remain true'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a rule that prevails still holds good, staying in force.

entries.clue: Give a lecture, showing how to dispense Sellotape? (4,7,3,1,5)

blocks.note: to scold, not to teach a class
read literally, the idiom describes pulling a length off a roll of tape

annotation.surface: A lecturer demonstrates how to use a roll of sticky tape.
annotation.walkthrough: Sellotape is the British brand name for clear sticky tape. The second definition reads the idiom literally: you tear some off a strip.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to tear someone off a strip is to scold them, and literally it is what you do with tape.

entries.clue: Film, according to mother, carried by star (8)

indicatorNotes.carried by: what is carried by something sits inside it, so PER MA goes into SUN

blocks.note: per = according to, as in 'per the rules'

annotation.surface: Mother's view of a film, carried by its star.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Star' looks like the film's lead actor, and it is the Sun.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Superman is the 1978 film starring Christopher Reeve, among later ones.

entries.clue: Second group hit hotel room to get sweaty (5,4)

blocks.note: H = hotel in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A second band played a hit in a hotel room, sweating.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Group' and 'hit' suggest a pop band and its chart success; they are a team and a strike.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: a steam bath is a room filled with steam where you go to sweat.

entries.clue: Page stolen and old picture taken (5)

annotation.surface: A page and an old picture have been stolen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Taken' seems to repeat 'stolen', but it belongs to the definition: a picture taken with a camera.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: you take a photo, so 'picture taken' fits.

entries.clue: Sophisticated reconnaissance, covering her and husband separately? (9)

indicatorNotes.covering: a cover goes round something, so RECCE wraps the other pieces
indicatorNotes.separately: done separately means apart, so HER and H go in at two different places

annotation.surface: Someone spies on a woman and her husband separately.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Separately' is the key: the two inserts do not sit together but go into the recce at different points, one in each gap.
annotation.definitionFit: A borrowed French word: recherché means refined and exquisite, so sophisticated in taste.

entries.clue: Doctor in a car heading for Freetown, relatively local? (7)

indicatorNotes.Doctor: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.heading for: the head of a word is its first letter, here of Freetown

annotation.surface: A doctor drives to Freetown, where he is fairly local.
annotation.walkthrough: Freetown is the capital of Sierra Leone, so something African is local to it in a broad sense; the question mark marks that stretch.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic stretch: anything from the same continent as Freetown is local to it, relatively speaking.

entries.clue: A transport company’s fleet operates badly (6)

blocks.note: a bus company's fleet is its buses

annotation.surface: A bus company's fleet is badly run.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface complains about a poorly run bus service; the definition is a verb, to misuse.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to abuse a machine or privilege is to misuse it, operate it badly.

entries.clue: Lounge in northerly inn burst into flames (5,2)

indicatorNotes.in: one thing in another sits inside it, so LAZE goes inside the inn
indicatorNotes.northerly: in a down entry, going north means reading upwards, so PUB becomes BUP

blocks.note: a pub is an inn; read northwards it becomes BUP

annotation.surface: A lounge in a northern inn catches fire.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lounge' looks like the pub's lounge bar, but it is the verb, to laze.
annotation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb: fire that blazes up flares suddenly, as when something bursts into flames.

entries.clue: Curved branch splits from the bottom, the noise waking you? (6,3)

indicatorNotes.from the bottom: in a down entry, reading from the bottom up reverses the word

blocks.note: rips = splits; read from the bottom it is SPIR
an alarm is what wakes you

annotation.surface: A curved tree branch splits from its base with a noise loud enough to wake you.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a tree cracking; the answer is astronomy, one of the curved arms of a spiral galaxy.
annotation.definitionFit: A description from astronomy: the curved branches of stars winding out of a galaxy are its spiral arms.

entries.clue: Potentially profit from deputy taking in Roman’s clothing (5,2,4)

indicatorNotes.taking in: to take something in is to admit it inside, so STAND IN holds TOGA

blocks.note: the toga was the Roman garment

annotation.surface: A deputy who takes in a Roman's clothes might make money from it.
annotation.walkthrough: The garment lands inside the hyphenated word for a deputy, so the word breaks of the wordplay do not match the answer's.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: you stand to gain when a profit is possible but not yet made, hence 'potentially'.

entries.clue: Programme you can stand listening to? (9,7)

annotation.definition: Programme you can stand listening to?

blocks.note: the surface offers a programme you can bear, one you can tolerate
taken literally, 'stand' means being on your feet while you listen

annotation.surface: Someone recommends a programme they can bear to hear.
annotation.walkthrough: At a promenade concert, like the BBC Proms in London, part of the audience stands, so 'can stand' is literal.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic reading: a promenade concert is a programme of music heard by a standing audience.

entries.clue: Thin coat secretary can pad in the middle (6)

indicatorNotes.in the middle: only what sits in the middle of pad is taken, its centre letter

annotation.surface: A secretary pads out a thin coat in the middle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb about what the secretary is able to do; it is a tin.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a patina is a thin film or sheen that forms over a surface.

entries.clue: To improve best mark immediately, correct an error (3,3,6,8)

blocks.note: to set the record is to beat the previous best

annotation.surface: An athlete sets out to beat the best mark straight away and fix a mistake.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as sport, but the wordplay and definition split the idiom at 'straight'.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to put an account right after a mistake has spread.

entries.clue: Chef’s fans given 50 per cent off, in addition (5)

indicatorNotes.given 50 per cent off: a half-price cut: half of the ten letters are removed

blocks.note: a kitchen's extractor fans; the last five letters go

annotation.surface: A chef's fans get a half-price discount on top.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fans' suggests admirers of the chef, but they are the extractors that clear kitchen smoke.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym used as an adverb: paid extra means paid in addition.

entries.clue: European rocket redirected following quiet chat (7)

indicatorNotes.redirected: sent the other way, so E ZOOM is reversed
indicatorNotes.following: what follows comes after, so the reversed piece goes after SH

annotation.surface: A European rocket changes course after a quiet word.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rocket' reads as a space launcher, but it is the verb, to zoom.
annotation.definitionFit: A Yiddish borrowing: to shmooze is to chat, often to win someone over.

entries.clue: Conservative in the same plane with US president (9)

annotation.surface: A Conservative flies on the same aircraft as a US president.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plane' looks like an aircraft; it is the flat plane of geometry, so 'in the same plane' is LEVEL.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Grover Cleveland was the 22nd and 24th US president.

entries.clue: Old educational institution last to trial novel form of debate (9)

indicatorNotes.last to: the last of a word is its final letter, here the end of trial

blocks.note: poly = polytechnic, a type of British college that became a university in 1992

annotation.surface: A former college stages a trial of a new kind of debate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like 'new', and it is the book Emma.
annotation.definitionFit: A technical term: a polylemma is an argument offering several alternatives, all unwelcome, a dilemma with more horns.

entries.clue: Dog — the one we have — sweats (7)

annotation.surface: Our dog is panting and sweating.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sweats' is a verb meaning works hard, as in sweating over a task.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to sweat over something is to labour at it.

entries.clue: Barrel officer commanding twice rolled over, fair target? (7)

indicatorNotes.twice: something done twice happens two times, so OC is written out twice
indicatorNotes.rolled over: something rolled over ends up facing the other way, so the whole string reverses

blocks.note: a tun is a large cask
OC = officer commanding, two of them

annotation.surface: A barrel and a commanding officer roll over twice at a funfair.
annotation.walkthrough: The target is at a British fairground's coconut shy, where you throw balls to knock coconuts off stands.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition by example: at a coconut shy on a fairground, the coconut is what you aim at.

entries.clue: Lump of thickened skin on horse’s inner ear (7)

blocks.note: a cob is a sturdy horse

annotation.surface: A horse has a hard lump of skin inside its ear.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'ear' a horse's ear; it is an ear of maize, whose central core is the corncob.
annotation.definitionFit: A pun on ear: the corncob is the central core of an ear of maize.

entries.clue: Art gallery in favour of framing poster, say (5)

indicatorNotes.framing: a frame goes round a picture, so PRO goes round AD

blocks.note: a poster is one kind of ad

annotation.surface: A gallery supports framing a poster.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Framing' belongs in an art gallery, which hides its job as a container.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Prado is Spain's national art museum in Madrid.

entries.clue: Blank book in sale with no covers, worthless (5)

indicatorNotes.with no covers: a word's covers are its outside letters, so they are removed

blocks.note: sALe without its first and last letters
bum = worthless, as in a bum deal

annotation.surface: A blank book in a sale, missing its covers, is worthless.
annotation.walkthrough: A coverless book sounds worthless, but 'covers' belongs to 'sale'.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: an album starts as a book of blank pages for photos or stamps.

entries.clue: Sugar chorister’s fed to me (7)

indicatorNotes.fed to: food fed to someone goes into their mouth, so ALTOS goes inside ME

blocks.note: an alto is a chorister; the 's gives the S

annotation.surface: A choirboy's sugar is fed to me.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's reads as possession but supplies the S of ALTOS.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: maltose is the sugar formed from starch in malting grain.

entries.clue: Strange nature running through Ascot — Herne’s stag? (9)

indicatorNotes.running through: the answer runs through the words, across the gaps between them

annotation.surface: Something strange runs through Ascot: Herne the Hunter's stag.
annotation.walkthrough: Herne the Hunter is a horned ghost of Windsor Forest, near Ascot racecourse, so the surface is local folklore.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: otherness is the quality of being alien or different, a strange nature.

entries.clue: Shortening slalom, maybe naughty kid cut corners (5)

indicatorNotes.Shortening: to shorten a word is to cut its end, so SKI loses its last letter

blocks.note: slalom is one kind of ski race; SKI shortened
an imp is a naughty child

annotation.surface: A naughty child shortens a slalom run by cutting the corners.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cut corners' fits a ski run, which hides that it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to cut corners is to skimp, doing a job cheaply or hastily.

entries.clue: Cinema nuts divided by Oscar tributes (7)

indicatorNotes.nuts: crazy, so the letters of cinema are rearranged
indicatorNotes.divided by: something divided by a letter is split by it, so O goes into the rearranged letters

blocks.note: O = Oscar in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: Film fans are split by Oscar tributes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' belongs with cinema but is just the letter O; the answer is the plural of encomium.
annotation.definitionFit: A Latin plural: encomia are formal speeches or writings of praise, tributes.

entries.clue: Facetious lady impersonates saint after church (7)

annotation.surface: A joking woman mimics a saint after church.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Facetious' describes the word, not the lady: chapess is a jokey female form of chap.
annotation.definitionFit: A usage label: chapess is a jocular word for a woman, so 'facetious lady' describes it.

entries.clue: Temperature on Blue Nile turned boiling (9)

indicatorNotes.turned: the letters are turned into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, joined to T by 'on'

annotation.surface: The temperature on the Blue Nile turned boiling hot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boiling' is the literal sense of ebullient, from the Latin for bubbling up.
annotation.definitionFit: The literal, Latin sense: ebullient comes from ebullire, to boil up.

entries.clue: What creature with whiskers twists? (5)

indicatorNotes.twists: to twist something is to turn it round, so the letters reverse

annotation.surface: A riddle: what does a whiskered animal twist?
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a man twists the ends of his tache, British slang for a moustache.
annotation.definitionFit: An &lit: a moustached man, a creature with whiskers, twists the ends of his tache.

entries.clue: Prisoner’s fish helping mental process? (13)

blocks.note: con = convict; the 's gives the S
the ide is a freshwater fish

annotation.surface: A prisoner's fish serving helps his thinking.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Helping' looks like a verb, but it is a noun: a portion of food.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: careful thought is a mental process.

entries.clue: Number 10 notes admitting liability is harmful (7)

blocks.note: an IOU is a note admitting a debt

annotation.surface: Downing Street's notes admitting fault are damaging.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Number 10' reads as Downing Street, the Prime Minister's residence, but it splits into NO and X.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, often of fumes or gases that do harm.

entries.clue: Korean city a short distance east? Further (7)

blocks.note: an inch is a short distance

annotation.surface: A Korean city lies a short way east, and further still.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark ends one sentence and 'Further' starts another, so it is a separate piece.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Incheon is a South Korean port city, home to Seoul's main airport.

entries.clue: After leaving, cooler in rented address (4-6,3)

annotation.surface: After moving out, a cool box sits in the rented flat.
annotation.walkthrough: The pieces break across the words: POST-OFF-ICE-BOX, with ICEBOX straddling the hyphen and space.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: you pay the post office for a box, and mail sent to it makes it your address.

entries.clue: Make demands for the return of little angel lost on Mars (3,2,6)

annotation.definition: Make demands for the return of

indicatorNotes.lost: something lost is confused and astray, so ON MARS is rearranged

blocks.note: a putto is a cherub in Renaissance art

annotation.surface: Someone demands the return of a cherub lost on Mars.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Make demands for the return of' reads as part of the story; it is the definition, a whole phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to put someone to ransom is to hold them and demand payment for their return.

entries.clue: Authenticated resin brought back from SE France (9)

indicatorNotes.brought back: something brought back returns the way it came, so LAC is reversed

blocks.note: lac is a resin from insects, used for shellac; brought back it is CAL

annotation.surface: Genuine resin has been brought back from the south of France.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is the adjective for Provence, in France's south-east.
annotation.definitionFit: A place adjective: Provençal means from Provence, in south-east France.

entries.clue: Theatre-goer’s box containing old appley fruit seemed weighty (6,5)

indicatorNotes.containing: a box containing something holds it inside, so LOGE holds O MEDLAR

blocks.note: a loge is a theatre box
the medlar is a small brown fruit related to the apple

annotation.surface: A theatre box holds some old, apple-like fruit that seems heavy.
annotation.walkthrough: The medlar is an old-fashioned fruit eaten when half-rotten; 'appley' points to its apple family.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a worry that loomed large seemed important, weighing on the mind.

entries.clue: Silk turned oily by cheese (7)

indicatorNotes.turned: something turned faces the other way, so FAT reads backwards

blocks.note: fat = oily, greasy; turned, it reads TAF

annotation.surface: A silk garment got greasy from cheese.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Oily by cheese' sounds like a stain, but it is FAT reversed placed beside FETA.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: taffeta is a crisp woven fabric, classically of silk.

entries.clue: Ship’s French crew in rowing boat were stripped (9)

indicatorNotes.stripped: something stripped has its outer layer taken off, so were loses its outside letters

blocks.note: a rowing eight has eight oarsmen
wERe without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A French ship's crew were stripped in a rowing boat.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Ship' means 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a freighter is a ship built to carry cargo.

entries.clue: Excite son’s greed, showing high rate of interest? (9)

indicatorNotes.Excite: to excite is to stir up, so the letters are stirred

annotation.surface: A son's greed shows up as charging a high rate of interest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'High rate of interest' sounds like greedy moneylending, which fits 'greed'; here interest means attention.
annotation.definitionFit: A pun on interest: someone absorbed in a thing shows a high degree of interest in it.

entries.clue: Walkway crew limp across quietly (9)

indicatorNotes.across: LANK is laid across P, like a board over a gap, so it follows P

blocks.note: a gang is a crew of workers

annotation.surface: A crew limps quietly across a walkway.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Limp' reads as the crew hobbling, but it is an adjective meaning lank.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a gangplank is the movable walkway for boarding a ship.

entries.clue: Sandwich unfinished but remains fresh (9)

indicatorNotes.unfinished: something unfinished lacks its end, so but loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.fresh: new, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: An unfinished sandwich stays fresh.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Remains' looks like a verb, but it is fodder; the sandwich is a long filled roll, a mainly American name.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a submarine, or sub, is a long filled bread roll, a kind of sandwich.

entries.clue: Look after marine as well as you’re told (3,2)

indicatorNotes.you’re told: what you are told, you hear, so the sound counts, not the spelling

annotation.surface: A marine is ordered to look after things too.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Marine' looks like a soldier; it is the adjective, of the sea.
annotation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb: to see to a job is to deal with it, look after it.

entries.clue: Upright attached to goal (2,3)

blocks.note: on = attached to, as in a handle on a door
an end is a goal, an aim

annotation.surface: A goalpost upright is fixed to the goal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upright' and 'goal' suggest a goalpost; the definition is the phrase for standing vertically.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a box stood on end is upright, balanced on its short side.

entries.clue: Musician’s fairly slowly cycling after Italian poet (7)

indicatorNotes.cycling: letters cycle round, moving from the front to the back

blocks.note: andante is a musician's term for a moderately slow tempo; its opening AN moves to the end

annotation.surface: A musician plays at a gentle pace after reading an Italian poet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'After' means 'in the style of' here, not 'following'.
annotation.definitionFit: An adjective from a name: Dantean means in the manner of Dante, the Italian poet.

entries.clue: Word identification not hard in articles (7)

indicatorNotes.not: 'not hard' means without the H, so it is removed from THINGS
indicatorNotes.in: one thing in another sits inside it, so ID goes inside TINGS

blocks.note: articles = THINGS; H = hard is removed

annotation.surface: Identifying a word is easy in grammar articles.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Articles' sounds like grammar ('a', 'the'), but it means objects.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: word, as in 'send word', means news, and tidings is an old word for news.
annotation.definitionNote: 'Word' is singular in form but means news, like the plural tidings.

entries.clue: Dab oil in different places over spinning top (7)

indicatorNotes.in different places: letters put in different places are moved around

annotation.surface: Someone oils a spinning top in several spots.
annotation.walkthrough: A diabolo is an hourglass-shaped top spun on a string between two sticks.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the diabolo is a juggling toy, a top spun on a string.

entries.clue: Piece of ironmongery, however flimsy, lasts for long time (4,5)

indicatorNotes.lasts for: the lasts of words are their final letters

annotation.surface: A piece of hardware, however flimsy, lasts a long time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lasts' reads as endurance, but it instructs taking last letters. Ironmongery is British for hardware.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a butt hinge is a common door hinge, a piece of hardware.

entries.clue: Fowl clergyman raised turned brown (7)

indicatorNotes.raised: in a down entry, something raised reads upwards, so it reverses

blocks.note: a dean is a senior clergyman; raised, it reads NAED

annotation.surface: A clergyman raises a chicken that turned brown.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turned brown' sounds like roasting the fowl, but it means dyed with henna.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb from a dye: henna colours hair reddish-brown, so hennaed hair has turned brown.

entries.clue: Country inn with a great spread (9)

indicatorNotes.spread: letters spread about are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder; with is a joiner

annotation.surface: A country inn serves a great spread.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Country inn' reads as a rural pub; 'Country' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Argentina is one country, in South America.

entries.clue: Cross, maybe, in response to a tomato sauce (7)

blocks.note: a cross in football is a kind of pass
at = in response to, as in 'at his request'

annotation.surface: Someone is cross, perhaps, about a tomato sauce.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as angry; it is a football cross, a kind of pass.
annotation.definitionFit: An Italian cooking term: passata is sieved tomato, used as a sauce base.

entries.clue: For example, entreat nurses to continue without a break (5)

indicatorNotes.nurses: to nurse is to hold close, so SUE holds EG

blocks.note: to sue is to plead, entreat

annotation.surface: A plea to nurses to carry on without a rest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nurses' looks like hospital staff but is a verb, to cradle.
annotation.definitionFit: A musical term: to segue is to pass into the next piece with no pause.

entries.clue: Spaniard no longer serving — nothing left (5)

annotation.surface: A retired Spanish player has nothing left.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Serving' is a tennis pun: Rafael Nadal retired from tennis in 2024.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example with a pun: Rafael Nadal, the Spanish tennis great, no longer serves.

entries.clue: Upsetting part for Pavarotti, Domingo likewise (5)

indicatorNotes.Upsetting: in a down entry, to upset is to tip over, so the letters read upwards
indicatorNotes.part for: only a part of the following words is used

annotation.surface: Pavarotti was upset over a role, and so was Domingo.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Part' sounds like an opera role, which suits the two tenors, but it signals a hidden answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: ditto means the same again, likewise.

entries.clue: Give agent a chair for military update (6)

blocks.note: 'Give ... a chair' means sit someone down; the phrase wraps round 'agent'
a rep is a sales agent

annotation.surface: An agent is offered a seat for a military briefing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Give a chair' wraps round 'agent': sit the rep down.
annotation.definitionFit: A military abbreviation: sitrep is short for situation report, an update on the ground.

entries.clue: Large gnat in mouth could be serious (2,8,6)

indicatorNotes.could be: the letters could be something else, rearranged

annotation.surface: Swallowing a large gnat could be serious.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is itself true, which makes the anagram hard to notice.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: something that is no laughing matter is serious, not to be joked about.
annotation.definitionNote: 'Serious' is an adjective; the answer is a noun phrase used after 'is' the same way.

entries.clue: Head of maintenance one calls getting stuck in the bog (6)

indicatorNotes.Head of: the head of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: The head of maintenance phones when he gets stuck in the toilet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bog' is British slang for toilet, which is the surface picture; the definition uses the marsh sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb from a noun: mire is boggy ground, so miring is sinking into it.

entries.clue: I say “Pirate king” like Spooner would (4,4)

indicatorNotes.like Spooner would: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

blocks.note: Captain Hook, the pirate in Peter Pan
swap the H and L sounds

annotation.surface: A man exclaims about a pirate king the way Spooner would.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pirate king' suggests the Pirate King of Gilbert and Sullivan, but it is two words: HOOK and LEAR.
annotation.definitionFit: An exclamation: 'I say!' and 'look here!' both demand attention.

entries.clue: Young swimmer whose kick is developing? (7)

annotation.definition: Young swimmer whose kick is developing?

blocks.note: the surface offers a child in swimming lessons
read literally, the creature has not yet grown the legs to kick with

annotation.surface: A young swimmer is still working on their leg kick.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a child learning to swim; a tadpole is literally growing its back legs.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic reading: a tadpole is a young frog that swims while its legs are still forming.
